title: Private control plane DNS cache divergence caused API split-brain and routing failures
creator: Priya Singh
description: Summary: On 2026-03-09 18:07 UTC a subset of Private/VPC control planes began returning intermittent 502/504s for internal orchestration APIs. This escalated into a degraded reconciliation loop for private deploy agents, causing failed health checks, delayed autoscaling, and client-side retries. Impact: ~12 customer private deployments experienced control-plane latencies >10s and temporary write failures; two customers reported failed on-prem upgrades during the window. Root cause: a DNS cache divergence between the private control-plane proxy and the orchestrator process on nodes. After a rolling network config change, expired negative/TTL entries were evicted inconsistently across processes; some proxies continued to use stale A records, while others resolved to newly promoted control-plane endpoints. This caused a transient split-brain where requests were routed to incompatible control-plane replicas that could not route KV cache updates, producing reconciliation failures and increased error rates. Contributing factors: (1) our internal DNS caching library had per-process caching with no cache-coordination or short-lived invalidation, (2) the control-plane routing table relied on DNS for endpoint discovery without a quick health-aware fallback, and (3) the rolling network change (MTU and NAT rule tweak) caused brief DNS resolution errors that exposed the caching issue. Mitigation applied during incident: (a) emergency rollback of the network change in the affected region, (b) force-restart of the control-plane proxy processes to flush caches, (c) temporary routing policy to prefer stable control-plane replica IPs (bypassing DNS) for critical reconciliation lanes. Post-incident state: All affected customers recovered by 2026-03-09 19:05 UTC. We observed no data loss; only transient failed writes and increased tail latency. The incident is classified as SEV2 for customer impact and operational risk.
action_items: 1) Short-term: Add process-level health checks that trigger DNS cache flush on non-zero DNS errors. Owner: Miguel Torres. ETA: 2026-03-18.
2) Medium-term: Implement coordinated DNS cache invalidation service for private control-plane processes (centralized invalidation via local IPC). Owner: Aisha Patel. ETA: 2026-04-08.
3) Medium-term: Add deterministic fallback to static control-plane replica IPs (configurable per-deployment) when DNS resolution variance detected. Owner: Liam O'Connor. ETA: 2026-03-31.
4) Long-term: Migrate control-plane service discovery to a health-aware registrator (gRPC-based) with built-in TLS pinning to avoid routing by DNS alone. Owner: Priya Singh. ETA: 2026-05-15.
5) Reliability: Add synthetic canary that simulates TTL churn and verifies reconciliation under DNS flapping. Owner: Reliability Team (assigned: Noor Khan). ETA: 2026-04-01.
6) Runbook: Create an incident runbook section for DNS cache divergence with playbook steps (detect, force-flush, route-failover, rollback). Owner: Miguel Torres. ETA: 2026-03-17.

7) Observability: Add per-process DNS resolution metrics (cache-hit, cache-miss, resolution-error-rate) and alert when divergence between processes > 5%. Owner: Observability Team (assigned: Samira Chen). ETA: 2026-03-25.
8) Compliance: Document the emergency rollback rationale and notify impacted customers with timeline and remediation summary. Owner: Customer Success (assigned: Carlos Rivera). ETA: 2026-03-14.
